transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Hi, yeah, thank you. Um, I'm mainly here because my sleep has basically just... fallen apart. I’ll lie in bed in my apartment for hours with my laptop closed, just staring. Which, by the way, I just bought this new mattress for the apartment because I thought maybe that was the problem—it was one of those memory foam ones you buy online that comes vacuum-sealed in a tiny box? It took like three days to fully expand and my whole bedroom smelled like factory chemicals for a week, it was a whole ordeal. 

But anyway, even on the new bed, I just lie there mentally rechecking everything. Work deadlines, my tuition payments, class assignments... I'm taking some extra classes right now to help with my job as an analyst, and the billing department at the university is completely disorganized. I had to call them three times last week just to get a receipt, and the girl on the phone sounded like she had no idea what system they even use. So my brain is just looping all of that all night. And even when I actually do manage to sleep, I wake up feeling like my brain never really turned off at all.
Have you experienced or witnessed any traumatic event recently or in the past that has been affecting your sleep or causing you ongoing distress?

No, I... I haven't been through anything traumatic like that. No car accidents or, you know, anything terrible. Honestly, my life is pretty boring on paper. I mostly just go to work and take my classes. Oh, speaking of driving though, the traffic near my office lately has been an absolute nightmare. They're doing this massive construction project on the main overpass, and I swear they've had the right lane closed for like six months. The other day, I was stuck behind this truck carrying... I don't know, gravel or something? And every time he hit a bump, little rocks would bounce off the back, and I was just terrified one was going to crack my windshield. Windshields are so expensive to replace now, and my insurance deductible is ridiculous because I changed my plan last year to try and save a little money on the premium. But anyway, no, nothing traumatic. Just the usual daily stuff, I guess.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried most days, even when there isn’t a specific problem happening at that moment?

Yeah, pretty much every day. It's like my mind just never stops running, even when nothing is actually wrong right that second. Like, I'll be sitting there and suddenly I'm worrying if I'm falling behind on my projects at work, and then that jumps to whether taking these extra classes is just a massive waste of money. Which, honestly, the cost of tuition is insane right now. I was looking at my student loan portal the other day, and the interest rate on one of my older loans just adjusted, and I spent like two hours trying to figure out if I should consolidate them or just pay extra on the principal. I even made this whole color-coded spreadsheet in Excel—I love Excel, I use it for everything at work as an analyst, it's so satisfying when the formulas work perfectly. 

But yeah, I just spiral. I start worrying my family is going to think I can't handle my life, and suddenly every tiny little bump in the road feels like it's going to completely ruin my entire future. It's exhausting.
Do you notice any physical symptoms, like restlessness, muscle tension, or feeling fatigued, even when you haven't been physically active?

Yeah, actually, I'm just so tired all the time. By midafternoon at the office, I feel completely drained. Like, even just answering an email or walking to the subway after work takes so much effort. Speaking of the subway, they just changed the schedule on my line, and it is a total mess. I waited on the platform for twenty minutes yesterday, and it was so hot down there. There was this guy playing a saxophone, which usually I don't mind, but he only knew like two songs and just kept looping them. And the acoustics in those stations just make everything echo so loudly. I read somewhere that the city was supposed to upgrade the ventilation systems in the stations, but I guess they ran out of budget. Typical, right? 

But anyway, yeah, I'm just exhausted. Even when I try to rest on the weekend, it doesn't seem to give me my energy back at all. I just feel heavy and wiped out.
